title: His mother arrives in Ottumwa with a husband he did not know about
summary: He sent for his mother, who stepped off the train with a new husband; Gus was furious, then found them a furnished house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, but I'd always send my mother --
Did you put it away?
I'd send my mother money, see.
Did you? That was nice, that was good, yeah.
Yeah. I sent for my mother to come to Ottumwa.
You did?
Her and her husband. So they came to Ottumwa.
Oh, wasn't that nice? Well, how long were you there?
I was there a year, because I left in the latter part of '37, to go join McShann.
To MacShan. Well, did your mother and your stepfather stay on?
Well, like, when she came there, I didn't know she had married again. And I met her at the train station. She got off the train and so did he. But I didn't pay him any mind.
No.
So he got off with the bags. She got off first -- he got off later with the bags and he was standing over here. And so I said, 'Where's your bags? Come on, so I can take you to where I'm staying.'
And so she said, 'Well, just a minute, that's my husband there.' I said, 'What old husband?' Just like that.
(Laughter.)
I didn't like that one bit.
She didn't tell you?
No, she didn't let me know, you know?
But she knew what you'd be like, huh?
I said, 'What old husband?' And she called him over and introduced him, and I just looked at him. I said, 'Are you sure you're married to her?' And I was mad as I could be, really. He said, 'Yes.'
Well, he has a nerve coming, when he

No, I didn't know anything about it, see. And he said, "I got papers to prove it." I said, "Well, I got to see them. That's it." And I carried them where I was staying, and I know they couldn't stay there. But I got them a room, got them really a whole house. And just lucky I knew someone that just had moved out of the house, but it was furnished. It was furnished, really. Everything was furnished.
And I got this house for them. And mouth stuck out, too, I just couldn't believe it. That really hurt me.
Yeah, you were surprised.
Well, you know.
Yeah, you sent for her --
She never told me that she'd gotten married. She kept that a secret on me.
Yeah. Had she been married long?
She'd been married for over a year. And I didn't know it. And it just hurt me.
Well, sure. And you thought you were helping her out and bringing her --
Well, but she still needed it, (Audible), I knew that, see.
Yeah.
It's always been that way, because I didn't care what I made, I would send my mother money.
Good, good.
One of those things. That was it.
Yeah.
Because that's the way I was brought up.
Yeah, and she brought you up.
She brought me up like that.
Yeah.
She never asked for anything.
No.
Never asked me for nothing, unless she really needed it, said, 'Son, I need such-and-such.' I would send it to her.
Yeah.
But I would send her things whether she needed or not.
Yeah.
So, --
